facts.text: Eastborough was conceived in the 1920s by British architect Burdon Hunter as an English village amid the Kansas prairie.
Eastborough and neighboring Woodlawn joined forces and incorporated as a third‑class city on June 1 1937, ending long‑standing disputes.
Eastborough earned a reputation as a “speed trap” because its main streets run at 20 mph, a full 33 percent slower than Wichita’s 30 mph limit.
The city’s 21 streets were laid out in an English‑style layout with winding drives, broad lawns, parks, and a lake, reflecting Hunter’s original vision.
Eastborough is an enclave completely surrounded by Wichita, making it a unique pocket of historic planning within the larger city.
The original 215‑acre tract that became Eastborough was developed by Alton H. and others, following Hunter’s design for a quaint village.
